title: Compatible horns in simplicial abelian groups admit fillers
statement:
Let $G:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}	o\mathrm{Ab}$ be a simplicial abelian group, with face homomorphisms $d_i$ and degeneracy homomorphisms $s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For every integer $n\geq1$, every $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and every family $a_i\in G_{n-1}$ indexed by $0\leq i\leq n$ with $i
e k$, assume, when $n\geq2$, that $d_i a_j=d_{j-1}a_i$ for all $i<j$ with $i,j
e k$. (For $n=1$ there are no compatibility equations.) Then there exists $u\in G_n$ such that $d_i u=a_i$ for every $i
e k$.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, lines 5755-5803; specialization to abelian groups, with the compatible-face description of a horn given explicitly in the first paragraph of its proof.

proof.text: The operators are those of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and all are homomorphisms. Applying the contravariant functor $G$ to [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity] gives $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$ whenever typed. We also use $d_i s_j=s_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$, $d_j s_j=d_{j+1}s_j=1$, and $d_i s_j=s_j d_{i-1}$ for $i>j+1$. These mixed identities follow directly from the defining order maps: $\delta_i(t)=t+\mathbf1_{t\geq i}$ and $\sigma_j(t)=t-\mathbf1_{t>j}$. In $\sigma_j\delta_i(t)$ substitute the first expression into the second. If $i<j$, the result is $t+\mathbf1_{t\geq i}-\mathbf1_{t\geq j}$, also the value of $\delta_i\sigma_{j-1}(t)$; if $i=j$ or $i=j+1$, the added and subtracted indicators agree, giving $t$; if $i>j+1$, the result is $t+\mathbf1_{t\geq i}-\mathbf1_{t>j}$, also the value of $\delta_{i-1}\sigma_j(t)$. Thus the respective order maps agree on every element; contravariance and preservation of identity give the asserted mixed identities. This is the elementary order-map computation of Stacks 0167(2)--(4), not an invocation of a reconstruction theorem.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof; additive specialization, with the relations of Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy.

proof.text: First handle $n=1$. There is exactly one prescribed face, say $a_i\in G_0$ with $i\ne k$. Set $u=s_0a_i$. Both $d_0s_0$ and $d_1s_0$ are the identity by Step 1, so $d_i u=a_i$. No face map with source $G_0$ or compatibility equation is used. Henceforth assume $n\geq2$.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof; additive specialization, with the relations of Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy.

proof.text: Restrict the horn family to $0\leq i<k$. For $i<j<k$, neither index is the missing index, so the original compatibility supplies exactly $d_i a_j=d_{j-1}a_i$. Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-prefix-correction] with the same $n\geq2$, $0\leq k\leq n$, and initial element $v=0\in G_n$. Its invariant at $r=k$ gives $d_i v_k=a_i$ for all $i<k$. This is precisely the starting hypothesis needed for the descending induction. If $k=0$, its initial and terminal element is $v_0=0$ and this hypothesis is empty. The prefix theorem imposes no condition on its initial element: the $r=0$ invariant has no indices, so starting at zero requires no vanishing assumption on $G$.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, second paragraph: ascending correction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-descending-correction] to the original horn family, with $v=v_k$. Its compatibility is the original compatibility; Step 3 supplies its only extra hypothesis, the prescribed lower faces of $v$. The resulting sequence starts with $w_n=v_k$, for which the upper-face condition $i>n$ is empty. At a transition $n\geq r>k$, $a_r$ is prescribed and $0\leq r-1\leq n-1$, so its correction $s_{r-1}(a_r-d_rw_r)$ is typed. The cited invariant preserves faces $i<k$ and $i>r$ and sets face $r$, yielding the next invariant. After $n-k$ transitions take $u=w_k$; the terminal invariant gives $d_i u=a_i$ for $i<k$ or $k<i\leq n$, exactly the desired faces. If $k=n$ there are zero transitions and $u=v_k$; if $k=0$ no lower-face assertion is needed.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, third paragraph: descending correction and its final invariant.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, additive specialization: explicit order-map identities and degree one, then assembly of the separately queued ascending and descending correction inductions.

lean.statement: theorem exists_horn_filler (G : SimplicialObject AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (n : ℕ) (k : Fin (n + 2)) (a : (i : Fin (n + 2)) → i ≠ k → G _⦋n⦌) (hcompat : match n, k, a with | 0, _, _ => True | m + 1, k, a => ∀ (i j : Fin (m + 2)), i ≤ j → ∀ (hi : i.castSucc ≠ k) (hj : j.succ ≠ k), G.δ i (a j.succ hj) = G.δ j (a i.castSucc hi)) : ∃ u : G _⦋n + 1⦌, ∀ (i : Fin (n + 2)) (hi : i ≠ k), G.δ i u = a i hi
